Epoch leader schedule creation with stake sorting, deduping, and weighted sampling.

# Purpose
`fd_epoch_leaders.c` implements the shared-memory object that stores the leader schedule for one epoch. The file defines the alignment and footprint helpers, then builds an `fd_epoch_leaders_t` object in caller-owned memory with [`fd_epoch_leaders_new`](<#fd_epoch_leaders_new>). That constructor validates the memory address, prepares the stake list, and, when `vote_keyed_lsched` is zero, sorts and deduplicates vote keys by `id_key` while adding duplicate stake values. It then sorts the final stake list by stake and key, which is the order needed for leader selection.

The file also creates the schedule itself. It uses `fd_wsample` with a ChaCha20-based RNG seeded from `epoch` to draw leader indices for each schedule slot, stores those indices in shared memory, and then copies the public keys into the same memory region after sampling is complete. An extra entry stores the indeterminate leader key for out-of-range samples. The remaining functions, [`fd_epoch_leaders_join`](<#fd_epoch_leaders_join>), [`fd_epoch_leaders_leave`](<#fd_epoch_leaders_leave>), and [`fd_epoch_leaders_delete`](<#fd_epoch_leaders_delete>), provide the standard shared-memory object interface and return the same memory pointer without extra cleanup.
